module purpose: neorv32_imem implements processor-internal instruction memory as either pre-initialized ROM or writable RAM, selected by IMEM_INIT. It derives a word index from the request address, optionally writes byte-enabled RAM data, captures addressed memory data in rdata, and returns data and acknowledge on the response bus while err is tied low.

use-case flows.value: word-index selection from the request address for IMEM access
byte-enabled RAM write of request data into internal IMEM when IMEM_INIT is false
addressed IMEM word loaded into rdata from ROM or RAM and returned on read responses
acknowledge response, qualified as read-only in ROM mode and as any strobe in RAM mode
read-enable and acknowledge cleared while rstn_i is low

conceptual assets.concept: IMEM word-address selection for the current access
conceptual assets.reasoning: The module computes `addr <= unsigned(bus_req_i.addr(addr_hi_c downto 2));` at line 101, and that index is then used for ROM fetches at line 81 and RAM byte writes/reads at lines 116, 119, 122, 125 and 128-131. Integrity matters because a wrong index updates or returns the wrong IMEM word. `alt_style_c` is fixed false at line 38, so the alternative delayed-address path using `addr_ff` at lines 92-95 and 142, 159-162 is not elaborated.

conceptual assets.concept: Writable IMEM contents in RAM configuration
conceptual assets.reasoning: Under `if not IMEM_INIT generate` (lines 106-165), write cycles store the four byte lanes of `bus_req_i.data` into `mem_ram_b0..3` when `bus_req_i.stb`, `bus_req_i.rw` and the corresponding `bus_req_i.ben` bit are asserted (lines 114-125). Those stored bytes are later read back into `rdata` at lines 128-131. Integrity matters because later reads must return the bytes previously accepted for that address and byte-enable pattern. Availability is also established because these byte-lane arrays hold state between clocked writes and are read again by the module.

conceptual assets.concept: Current IMEM read word buffered for response
conceptual assets.reasoning: `rdata` holds the currently selected IMEM word that the response path uses: in ROM mode `rdata <= mem_rom_c(to_integer(addr));` at line 81, and in RAM mode its byte lanes are loaded from `mem_ram_b0..3` at lines 128-131; `bus_rsp_o.data <= rdata when (rden = '1') else (others => '0');` at line 185 then uses this buffered word. Integrity matters because a read must deliver the addressed IMEM word. Availability is established because the active default implementation clocks this value on `clk_i`. Although the map also lists assignments at lines 95 and 159-162, RTL line 38 fixes `alt_style_c` to false, so those alternative paths are unreachable.

The module records whether the current request is a read with `rden <= bus_req_i.stb and (not bus_req_i.rw);` at line 176, and line 185 gates `bus_rsp_o.data` with that decision. Integrity matters because IMEM data must only be presented for read requests, not for other cycles. Availability is also established because `rden` is updated on each rising edge and reset to `'0'` at line 173.

conceptual assets.concept: Acknowledge decision for IMEM access completion
conceptual assets.reasoning: The response process resets acknowledge low at line 174, then in ROM configuration assigns `bus_rsp_o.ack <= bus_req_i.stb and (not bus_req_i.rw);` at line 178, and in RAM configuration assigns `bus_rsp_o.ack <= bus_req_i.stb;` at line 180. Integrity matters because request completion must follow these implemented conditions. No eligible structural reference survives the closed-set restrictions because this decision exists only on `bus_rsp_o.ack`, a field of the transport response record `bus_rsp_o`, and transport ports are excluded.
